methods.name: opt_in_asset
methods.desc: The application account must opt into the bond asset before it can custody bonds.

methods.name: register
methods.desc:
Publish an SLA. `max_staleness` and `max_latency_ms` are the bounds the
provider will later be judged against, committed by the provider itself.

methods.name: deposit_bond
methods.desc: Stake collateral. Grouped with the asset transfer that funds it.

methods.name: withdraw_bond
methods.desc: A provider may unstake at any time. Unstaking is itself a signal.

methods.name: submit_claim
methods.desc:
Prove that `provider` signed a response violating its own published SLA,
and settle it atomically: refund the caller, slash the provider, update the counters. Returns the micro units refunded.
The proof is self contained. The contract checks the provider's own signature over the response, and compares the timestamp the provider attested to against the staleness bound the provider itself published. Nobody has to be trusted, and nobody adjudicates.
Compensation is paid to Txn.sender, who must hold the signed response (only obtainable by paying for it) and be opted into the bond asset.

methods.name: record_success
methods.desc:
Attest verified good responses. Batched, because the demo makes many
calls and one transaction per call is pure noise.
This is the one number in the system that is an attestation rather than a proof: the operator is asserting it observed N good responses. It is deliberately separate from claim_count, which is proven on chain.

methods.name: noop
methods.desc: Budget padding. Grouped with submit_claim to pool opcode budget.
